In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah At-Tahrim

His saying, exalted is He: "O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?" (Qur'an 66:1), and the rest of the verse.

It has already been explained at the beginning of the surah before it how the Ummah relates to the address specifically directed to him ﷺ. There has been disagreement about the prohibition of what Allah made lawful for him: whether it was honey, or whether it was Maryah, his slave-girl ﷺ. Further clarification of the discussion of its ruling will come later.

His saying, exalted is He: "Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives?" (Qur'an 66:1). It clearly carries the meaning of reproach, as in His saying, exalted is He: "He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you perceive? Perhaps he would have purified himself" (Qur'an 80:1-3).

Both of these have a connection to the personal dimension, whether seeking the pleasure of the wives or seeking the appeasement of the leaders of Quraysh. This indicates that personal aims have no place in Islamic legislation.

By this we take the argument from the converse analogy (qiyas al-'aks) as clear evidence against the claim of those who say that his ﷺ having ordered 'A'ishah to perform the 'umrah from al-Tan'im was to console her, and that this is valid for no one other than her.

The point of the inference is that whoever has no right to prohibit what Allah has made lawful for him, seeking the pleasure of his wives, is not permitted to make lawful or allow what is not permitted, seeking their pleasure. This is clear and evident, and all praise is due to Allah.

As for the expiation of the oath (tahillat al-yamin) and the expiation for breaking an oath (kaffarat al-hanth), and other matters, their explanation has already been given by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, at his saying, exalted is He: "Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths" (Qur'an 2:225).

As for the true nature of the prohibition here, the type of expiation, and whether he ﷺ made expiation for it or Allah forgave him so that no expiation was needed, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has clarified this in Mudhakkirat al-Imla' at this verse.

(p-220) And in Adwa' al-Bayan, at His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of Surah Al-Ahzab: "And He did not make your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers" (Qur'an 33:4). This is because the scholars have some twenty opinions. He preferred the view that the prohibition is zihar, in accordance with what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates, and that the view following it is that it is an oath. He discussed the issue with its evidences there.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah At-Tahrim

His saying, exalted is He: "O Prophet" (Qur'an 66:1).

Along with His saying: "Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths" (Qur'an 66:2), the same difficulty arises in it.

The answer is what has preceded in Surah At-Talaq.

The Qur'anic phrase in the Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 4:

﴿If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have certainly swerved﴾.

Repentance is stated without qualification here, but it is qualified in the verse after it, as sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah), in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾ [At-Tahrim: 8].

The reality of sincere repentance, its conditions and its effects were explained earlier by the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and on him, at His saying: ﴿And repent to Allah all together, O believers﴾ [An-Nur: 31].

As for His saying, ﴿your hearts have certainly swerved﴾, the Shaykh said in his dictation: "(Saghat) means: inclined, was pleased, and loved what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked." (End of quote.)

He also said: "(Qulubukuma, 'your hearts') is in the plural, although it refers to two people, Hafsah and Aishah. It was said that this is because the meaning is known, and the plural is lighter than the dual when it is put in construct. It was also said that this is among the things cited as evidence that the minimum of the plural is two, as in the case of inheritance, in His saying: ﴿But if he has brothers﴾ [An-Nisa': 11]." (End of quote.)

The answer to the condition in His saying, "If you two repent," is omitted. Its estimated form is: "then that is obligatory upon you both, because your hearts have inclined to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ does not love." (End of quote.)

Al-Qurtubi estimated it as: "that is better for you," and the two meanings are close.

* *

His saying, ﴿And if you two back each other up against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers, and after that the angels are his supporters﴾.

Abu Hayyan said: The pause is on (mawlahu, "his protector"), and the guardianship (wilayah) is specific to Allah. Jibril is then the subject (mubtada'), and what follows is joined to it by conjunction, and (zahir, "supporters") is the predicate. In this reading, Jibril is mentioned twice: first specifically, and then generally. (End of quote.)

It was also said: the pause is on (Jibril), joined by conjunction to the name of Allah in guardianship. Then a new sentence begins with the righteous of the believers, and the angels are joined to them, and Jibril is included among them implicitly. (End of quote.)

According to the first pause, the placing of the righteous of the believers between Jibril and the angels is a notice of the high rank of the righteous believers, and a statement of their standing among the angels in general after Jibril. According to the second pause, there is in it the joining of Jibril to the name of Allah in guardianship with the conjunction "wa" (and). There is nothing in it that suggests a contradiction with the hadith concerning "thumma" (then), because the place of the conjunction is guardianship, and guardianship is a possible measure both from the creatures and from Allah, Exalted is He, as in His saying: ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ [Al-Anfal: 62]. This is because help comes from Allah and also comes from the servants, by way of taking the means: ﴿If you do not support him, then Allah has already supported him﴾ [At-Tawbah: 40].

As in His saying: ﴿And they support Allah and His Messenger﴾ [Al-Hashr: 8].

And His saying: ﴿Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 52]. This is unlike the context of the hadith, for it concerned the matter of will (mashi'ah), when a Bedouin said: "What Allah wills and you will." He said to him ﷺ: "Have you made me an equal to Allah? Say: what Allah alone wills." Because the reality of will belongs to Allah Exalted alone, as in His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [At-Takwir: 29], and as in His saying: ﴿Rather, to Allah belongs the command entirely﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 31], and as in His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command before and after﴾ [Ar-Rum: 4].

Among the subtle points in His saying, ﴿And if you two back each other up against him﴾, up to the end of what I heard from the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and on him, is that he said: The two who backed each other up against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were two women only, who conspired against him between themselves. Then the mention of those who support him against them came, each one mentioned in the verse: ﴿Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers and the angels﴾. This indicates the greatness of their scheming and the weakness of men before them. This was indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, your scheming is great﴾ [Yusuf: 28], whereas about the scheming of Satan He said: ﴿Indeed, the scheming of Satan is ever weak﴾ [An-Nisa': 76].

The poet expressed this with his saying:

Allah did not regard their scheming as great
except because they are what they are, what they are.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, penitent, worshipful, given to travel, previously married and virgins﴾.

In this there is an explanation that the excellence which Allah chooses for His Messenger ﷺ in women is those qualities of faith and righteousness.

There came the hadith: "Then you should choose the one who is religious, may your hands be rubbed with dust" (fa-'alayka bi-dhat al-din taribat yaminuk).

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A believing slave-woman is better than an idolatress, even though she should please you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221].

In placing the previously married women before the virgins here, in the context of giving choice, there is an indication of their precedence, although the hadith says: "Why not a virgin, who would delight you and whom you would delight?" and the women of Paradise, "no man or jinn has touched them before them." So there is in this the precedence of virgins. The exegetes have answered that this is only for variety, and that the previously married women are for this world while the virgins are for Paradise, like Maryam daughter of 'Imran. What appears, and Allah knows best, is that since the context was one of defending the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and alerting them to what befits his station with them, He mentioned the lofty qualities in religion and character, and placed the previously married women first, to make clear that the excellence in them is according to companionship and good conduct.

His saying: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you﴾ does not clarify whether he did divorce them or not, although "ʿasā" (it may be) from Allah implies certainty. But their divorce did not occur, as Allah explained in Surah al-Ahzab, that He gave them the choice between Allah and His Messenger and the life of this world and its adornment, so they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Hereafter, and so He did not divorce them, and did not give him in exchange wives better than them.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, explained this matter, along with the lawfulness of marriage for him and the prohibition of women after them to him, at His saying: ﴿O Prophet, We have made lawful to you your wives﴾ up to the verse [al-Ahzab: 50].

And His saying: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 51].

And His saying: ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty should please you﴾ up to the verse [al-Ahzab: 52].

He also explained the abrogating from the abrogated in that, in order to remove the appearance of contradiction from the verses of the Book.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today﴾.

Here He does not specify the kind of excuse-making that they were forbidden from, nor the reason why it was forbidden, nor its time. However, He, exalted is He, has specified the kind of their excuse-making in such verses as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these had misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

And like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then their discord will not be except that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Look how they have lied against themselves﴾ [al-An'am: 23].

And like His saying after it: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Oh, if only we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers"﴾ [al-An'am: 27]. This is an extreme form of excuse-making, but they were forbidden from it on the Day of Resurrection, as in His saying: ﴿when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Oh, if only we could be returned"﴾, meaning, to the worldly life.

They were forbidden from this excuse-making because it does not benefit them, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong, nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ [ar-Rum: 57].

And His saying: ﴿The Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 52].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾.

The reference was previously made to the words of the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) in explaining the types of repentance (tawbah) and the conditions for it being nasuh (sincere), at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you﴾ [an-Nur: 31].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their light runs before them and on their right hands﴾ to the end of the verse.

The explanation of this light and their state in it was previously given by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) in Surah "al-Hadid" at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands﴾ [al-Hadid: 12].

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ جاهِدِ الكُفّارَ والمُنافِقِينَ واغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ .

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them.﴾

فِيهِ الأمْرُ بِقِتالِ الكُفّارِ، والمُنافِقِينَ والغِلْظَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ، ومَعْلُومٌ أنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قاتَلَ الكُفّارَ، ولَمْ يُعْلَمْ أنَّهُ قاتَلَ المُنافِقِينَ قِتالَهُ لِلْكُفّارِ، فَما نَوَّعَ قِتالَهُ ﷺ لِلْمُنافِقِينَ وبَيَّنَهُ ؟ واللَّهُ تَعالى أعْلَمُ.

In it is the command to fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh toward them. It is known that the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the disbelievers, but it is not known that he fought the hypocrites in the same manner as he fought the disbelievers. So how did he vary his fighting against the hypocrites, and how did he explain it? And Allah, Exalted is He, knows best.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَجاهِدْهم بِهِ جِهادًا كَبِيرًا﴾ [الفرقان: ٥٢]، أيْ: بِالقُرْآنِ لِقَوْلِهِ قَبْلَهُ: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْناهُ بَيْنَهم لِيَذَّكَّرُوا فَأبى أكْثَرُ النّاسِ إلّا كُفُورًا ولَوْ شِئْنا لَبَعَثْنا في كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَذِيرًا فَلا تُطِعِ الكافِرِينَ وجاهِدْهم بِهِ جِهادًا كَبِيرًا﴾ [الفرقان: ٥٠] .

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And strive against them with it, a great striving﴾ [al-Furqan: 52], meaning: with the Qur'an, due to His statement before it: ﴿And We have certainly diversified it among them that they may remember, but most of the people refused except denial. And had We willed, We would have sent into every town a warner. So do not obey the disbelievers and strive against them with it, a great striving﴾ [al-Furqan: 50].

وَمَعْلُومٌ أنَّ المُنافِقِينَ كافِرُونَ، فَكانَ جِهادُهُ ﷺ لِلْكُفّارِ بِالسَّيْفِ ومَعَ المُنافِقِينَ بِالقُرْآنِ.

It is known that the hypocrites are disbelievers, so his (ﷺ) striving against the disbelievers was with the sword, and his striving against the hypocrites was with the Qur'an.

(p-٢٢٤)كَما جاءَ عَنْهُ ﷺ في عَدَمِ قَتْلِهِمْ؛ لِئَلّا يَتَحَدَّثَ النّاسُ أنَّ مُحَمَّدًا يَقْتُلُ أصْحابَهُ، ولَكِنْ كانَ جِهادُهم بِالقُرْآنِ لا يَقِلُّ شِدَّةً عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّيْفِ، لِأنَّهم أصْبَحُوا في خَوْفٍ وذُعْرٍ يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ، وأصْبَحَتْ قُلُوبُهم خاوِيَةً كَأنَّهم خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ، وهَذا أشَدُّ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ المُلاقاةِ بِالسَّيْفِ، والعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَعالى.

(p-224) As has come from him (ﷺ) regarding not killing them, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions. Rather, their striving against them with the Qur'an was no less severe upon them than the sword, because they became in fear and terror, reckoning every cry to be against them, and their hearts became hollow, as if they were propped-up pieces of wood. And this is harsher upon them than meeting with the sword. And knowledge is with Allah, Exalted is He.

The Almighty said: ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and the two husbands could not avail them anything against God.﴾

The exegetes (mufassirun) agree here that the betrayal (khiyanah) was not a marital one.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The wives of the prophets are protected from sin, but it was a betrayal of religion, by their not believing and by informing their peoples about those among them who believed along with their husbands." End of quote.

This statement of Ibn ʿAbbas may find support in the prohibition on marrying the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) after him, with the reason given that this would harm him, as in the Almighty's words: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of God, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53].

If their asking (from behind a screen) without a veil harms him, and marrying them after him is an enormity in the sight of God, then how much more so would be other than asking and other than marriage? The station of the prophets with God is far greater than that.

As for the Almighty's words: ﴿They could not avail them anything against God﴾, this shows that the marital bond benefits nothing in the presence of disbelief. God has also made clear what is more important than that in general kinship, as in His words: ﴿On a Day when wealth and children will not avail.﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 88]

And His words: ﴿On the Day when a man will flee from his brother, his mother and his father﴾, and the verse continues [ʿAbasa: 34–35].

God made these two women an example for those who disbelieve, and this (example) includes all relatives, as we have mentioned.

I heard from the Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, during one of his lectures, an extended discussion of this, and he mentioned the story of these two women, and the story of Abraham with his father, and of Noah with his son. He thus completed the aspects of kinship: wife with her husband, son with his father, and father with his son. He also mentioned the hadith: "O Fatimah, act, for I cannot avail you anything against God."

Then he said: Let the Muslim know that no one possesses the ability to benefit anyone on the Day of Resurrection, even the closest of relatives (p-225), except through faith in God, and through what God honours whomever He wills with, by way of intercession, as in the Almighty's words: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them﴾ [al-Tur: 21].

The Qur'an's verse: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people."﴾

In this example there is a clarification that corresponds to the earlier clarification and to its opposite meaning, namely that the believer is not harmed by keeping company with the disbeliever, just as the disbeliever is not benefited by keeping company with the believer. Regarding this example, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in *Mudhakkirat al-Imla'* (Memorandum of Dictation):

"The wife of Pharaoh, in her request, chose the goodness of the neighbour over the house." End of quotation.

That is, in her saying: ﴿Build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, the verse [al-Tahrim: 11].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Mary, the daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our Spirit﴾.

He, exalted is He, made clear the meaning of "the Spirit" by stating that it is Jibril (peace be upon him), in His saying: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit, and it took for her the form of a man in all respects﴾ [Maryam: 17], and it is Jibril.

This is like His saying: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down﴾, meaning Jibril brought down the Qur'an. In this verse there is also a refutation of the Christians, who use it as evidence that 'Isa (peace be upon him) is the son of Allah and of His Spirit, exalted is He far above that with a great exaltation. The explanation of this refutation is that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, uses the verb arsala (sent) transitively without a preposition, which indicates that what is sent can be sent by itself. This is a distinction among the people of the language, whereas what is sent along with something else, such as a message or a gift, is said with the preposition: "I sent to him with such-and-such" (arsaltu ilayhi bi-kadhā), as in His saying: ﴿And I am going to send them a gift﴾ (the verse), [al-Naml: 35].

A gift is not sent by itself, and similarly ba'atha (to send/raise): you say, "I sent the camel away from its place" (ba'tu al-ba'ir min makanihi), "I sent an envoy" (ba'tu mab'ūthan), and "I sent with a message" (ba'tu bi-risāla).

Secondly, His saying: ﴿So it took for her﴾ — the word "Spirit" is feminine, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why, when it reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 83-84], where the verb is feminine in balaghat (it reached). Here, however, the pronoun is masculine, referring back to Jibril.

His saying: ﴿So it took for her the form of a man in all respects﴾ — and had it been from the Spirit of Allah, as the Christians maintain, there would have been no need for this taking of form.

Thirdly, His saying to her: ﴿I am only a messenger of your Lord﴾ [Maryam: 19], and the messenger of her Lord is Jibril (peace be upon him), not His Spirit, exalted is He.

Fourthly, His saying: ﴿to give you a pure boy﴾ [Maryam: 19], and He did not say "to give you a spirit from Allah."

From this also is His saying, exalted is He, to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay﴾ [Sad: 71], meaning Adam (peace be upon him): ﴿And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit﴾ [al-Hijr: 29], i.e., I breathed into him the spirit by which there is life: ﴿So fall down to him in prostration﴾ [al-Hijr: 29]. So if the Spirit were from Allah, Adam would have been more deserving of it than 'Isa, since He did not mention sending a messenger to him. And He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of 'Isa with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 59]. Likewise 'Isa (peace be upon him), when the angels gave her good news of him: ﴿She said, "My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?" He said, "Thus Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is"﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 47]. So each of Adam and 'Isa, He, exalted is He, said to him, "Be," and he was. And Allah knows best.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she was among the devout ones (al-qanitin)﴾.

It is not hidden that what comes to the mind is that a woman is not among the men, and He, exalted is He, did not say "among the devout women (al-qanitat)."

The answer is the consensus of the people of the Arabic language on giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine in the plural. So when He wished to make clear that Maryam was among the devout servants of Allah, and among them were males and females, He gave precedence to the masculine, as is required in the Arabic language. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, you were among the sinners (al-khati'in)﴾ [Yusuf: 29], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, she was of a disbelieving people﴾ [al-Naml: 43].
